newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia pays off most of its wage arrears - MinFin.
newsitem.headline: Russia pays off most of its wage arrears - MinFin.

text.p: Russia's federal government has paid off most of its wage arrears to public sector employees and the military, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.
"As of August 15, the Finance Ministry has a tiny debt on back wages -- about 50 billion roubles ($8.69 million)," Viktoriya Kotova of the ministry's Economic Expert Group said.

President Boris Yeltsin has ordered the government to pay off 7.7 trillion roubles in wages to public employees by 1998, including 5.2 trillion roubles in back wages to the military before September 1.
Kotova said the state's debt to the military was now about 10 billion roubles.
"We shall see next month what happened in reality -- maybe the military will come to us with a stretched hand again," she said.
She said the Defense Ministry, unlike other ministries, had the right to decide how to use government money allocated for back wages.

The government has made paying off wage arrears one of its priorities. Last month it sold a quarter of the national telecoms Svyazinvest and a voting stake in Norilsk Nickel metals producer to raise funds for such ends.
But the latest payments do not mean the government can rest in peace.
Last month the Finance Ministry said the government owed companies about 76 trillion roubles in unpaid bills.
